rule_labels.heuristic: A common multiplier heuristic (V10/raw, no gates)

spread_band: No p5-p95 band: the lines come from one synthetic world, and a spread over generator seeds is not computed yet (to measure).
title: Hand GRACE a Budget

backtest_sweep.kind: Simulated: true NPV per budget dollar at each solved budget of the sweep, each budget filled on its own (greedy fills are not nested).
backtest_sweep.lie: A sweep cell that differed from the standalone run would mean two different backtests (guard: test_sweep_cell_equals_standalone_run).
backtest_sweep.question: Does the rule order hold at every budget, or only at the one quoted?

batch_list.kind: Counted and simulated: the rule's own fill at this budget in buy order; predicted NPV is the engine's, true NPV is closed-form at the planted gem rate and true prices (synthetic truth); red rows are the generator's planted errors.
batch_list.lie: A batch interpolated between solved budgets would list cards no run bought, because greedy fills are not nested; every list is a solved run (guard: test_page_batches_equal_the_backtest_picks in tests/test_viz.py).
batch_list.question: Which cards does the rule actually buy at this budget, and which of them carry junk feed prices?

corruption_leakage.kind: Counted: planted-error cards in the batch over batch size, and their share of the capital spent, against the liquid universe's planted base rate.
corruption_leakage.lie: It would flatter the gates if junk cards were scored at their junk prices; they are scored at the base card's true prices (guard: test_junk_plants_true_prices_are_the_base_card).
corruption_leakage.question: How much of the budget goes to cards whose feed prices are junk?

oracle_value_captured.kind: Simulated: closed-form expected NPV at the generator's planted gem rates and true prices (synthetic truth), divided by the exact-knapsack oracle's batch.
oracle_value_captured.lie: It would lie if the oracle were not the best batch (guard: the oracle-bound tests in tests/test_backtest.py); it scores the generator against itself, so the rule order is the claim, not the dollars.
oracle_value_captured.question: Of the money a perfectly informed buyer could make with this budget, how much does the ranking find?

pick_optimism.kind: Simulated: mean predicted p10 minus mean planted p10 of the picks, and predicted batch NPV minus true batch NPV (synthetic truth).
pick_optimism.lie: It would hide the pop-bias caveat if the truth reused the selection-boosted or predicted rates; every universe row's true NPV is recomputed from the planted latent rate and true prices, and a control shows the predicted rate gives other values (guard: test_universe_true_npv_is_recomputed_from_the_truth). It is reported, never tuned away.
pick_optimism.question: On the cards a rule actually buys, how much rosier is the engine than the truth?

regret_and_npv_per_budget_dollar.kind: Simulated: oracle true NPV minus the rule's true NPV, and the rule's true NPV divided by the budget B (synthetic truth).
regret_and_npv_per_budget_dollar.lie: Dividing by dollars spent would reward a rule that leaves cash idle, and an overspent budget would inflate it (guards: test_denominator_is_the_budget, test_no_rule_overspends_the_budget).
regret_and_npv_per_budget_dollar.question: How many dollars does each rule leave on the table at this budget?
